git_tools.Description: Git on the bound project or vault, with any host (GitHub, GitLab, a company server): status, fetch, pull, log, diff, add, commit, push, branch, checkout, stash, restore across its repos (auto-discovered), plus git_clone to clone a repo into the project.

filesystem_tools.Description: Work with files: preview, read, list, search, find, edit, write, and deliver a file to the user as a download. read_file opens any file by what it is; Word, Excel, PDF and PowerPoint files each also have their own group (docx_tools, xlsx_tools, pdf_tools, pptx_tools) with readers, writers and editors. Every conversation has a working folder of its own, ready to use: write a file there and give it to the user with deliver_file. A bound project's files persist; the working folder is deleted with the conversation. You never need to set it up first.

coding_tools.Description: Build the current project to verify edits compile.

memory_tools.Description: Read and write Ari's personal brain (memory graph) — never through the generic filesystem tools. search_brain finds notes by title/alias/content — returns 'title — name' pairs. recall_memory reads the full content of a note by that name. create_memory adds a new note (fails if the name already exists); edit_memory replaces an existing note's content (fails if the name does NOT exist — and optionally renames/retypes it); delete_memory removes one. All three take a commit_message explaining what changed and why, and commit to the brain git repo immediately, one commit per note. neighbours shows graph connections around a note. memories_on gives everything stored for one calendar day. These tools access Ari's own stored memories, not a project filesystem.

vault_tools.Description: Search an Obsidian note graph within the bound project (regex, no index). Only useful when the project is an Obsidian vault — calling this on a code repository will return nothing. For searching your own memory, use search_brain / recall_memory instead.

project_tools.Description: List, create, rename, bind, and set the filesystem path of projects — the workspaces (code repos or note vaults) a conversation can be scoped to. Use this for any request to start/open/make a new project, workspace, or "project file" — that phrase means a new project, not a file inside one. If the user names a specific directory on their machine, confirm the exact path with them, then pass it to create_project (new project) or set_project_path (existing project) — never RemoteFs, which needs a connected desktop app and can't be pointed anywhere from chat.

calendar_tools.Description: ARI's own calendar. create_event adds context (working hours, a birthday, a trip) that is never acted on by itself. create_reminder schedules a real turn to fire later — write its prompt as an instruction to your future self, not the final wording. Both support repeat (daily/weekly/monthly/yearly, optionally an end date or count). list_events looks forward or backward from today by a signed day count. delete_entry removes either kind by id.

persona_tools.Description: Propose a change to your own persona. Load this when the user criticises HOW you replied — your tone, a verbal tic, a habit they find annoying — since promising to change does nothing on its own; your persona is what actually drives your behaviour.

image_tools.Description: Generate images using Stable Diffusion via ComfyUI. Supports text-to-image and img2img (pass reference_images from the user's attachments to guide composition). Prefer higher denoise (0.9–1.0) for creative freedom; lower (0.5–0.75) to stay close to a reference. Generating only shows you the result — call present_image afterward to reveal it to the user, or retry with a revised prompt if it's wrong.

web_tools.Description: Search the web and read web pages. Use for current events, factual lookups, or anything time-sensitive.

shell_tools.Description: Run commands and programs on the server Ari runs on: shell runs a command (and can start long jobs in the background), shell_job checks on or stops those jobs, run_code runs a short Python, JavaScript or bash program and returns what it prints. The owner approves anything that isn't read-only. For the user's own computer use run_command.

browser_tools.Description: A real web browser: browser opens a page, takes a screenshot you can look at, reads its text, clicks, types and scrolls. Use it to see how a website actually looks, to use pages that need JavaScript, and to check a site you've built.

task_tools.Description: Keep a checklist for a multi-step job so no step is forgotten (todo), and see or stop the tools you started in the background (jobs).

chat_tools.Description: Read other conversations when you're missing context: list_chats shows the recent ones, read_chat reads the latest messages of one, search_chats finds where something was said across all of them.

skill_tools.Description: Your own how-to notes: list_skills, read_skill, write_skill, delete_skill. Save one when you work out something worth repeating; check them before starting something you may have done before.

authoring_tools.Description: Write tools of your own. tool_docs explains the format, write_tool compiles a tool you wrote, test_tool tries it, read_tool and list_my_tools show what exists, delete_tool removes one. Use these when you need a capability you don't have. Plugins too: write_plugin, test_plugin, read_plugin, list_my_plugins, delete_plugin, with plugin_docs to read first.

subagent_tools.Description: Run subagents: spawn_agent starts one on a goal in the background with a subset of your loaded tools, wait_for_agent holds your reply open until they report back, cancel_agent stops one. Use for side tasks that need several tool calls, or to work on two things at once.

docx_tools.Description: Word documents (.docx): read_docx opens one (pages, find), write_docx creates one from Markdown (CVs, letters, reports), edit_docx replaces, deletes or appends text and keeps the formatting. The user's own file is never changed in place; edits go to a copy. Give the result to the user with deliver_file.

visual_tools.Description: Show a visual in the chat itself: show_visual displays HTML you write (a chart, diagram, table, timeline, calculator or small interactive page) under your message. Use it when a picture or something interactive explains better than words.

image_tools.Description: Pictures: ocr reads the text out of an image or a scanned PDF, edit_image resizes, crops, rotates, adds text, adjusts or converts a picture. To look at a picture and understand it, open it with read_file; to generate one use generate_image.

convert_tools.Description: Convert a document between formats: convert_document turns Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV, Markdown, HTML, text or a picture into md, txt, html, pdf, docx, csv or xlsx. Text, headings, lists and tables carry over; exact layout does not.

ssh_tools.Description: Other machines over SSH: ssh lists the machines the owner has saved, runs a command on one (each command is approved), copies files to and from it, and saves new machines. Key-based logins only; owner chats only.

chart_tools.Description: Draw charts as PNG pictures: make_chart turns CSV data into a bar, line, area, pie, scatter or histogram chart. Put the picture into a Word document, PDF or deck with ![caption](chart.png), or deliver it.

pdf_tools.Description: PDFs: read_pdf opens one (pages, find), write_pdf creates one from Markdown, pdf_merge joins PDFs, pdf_extract_pages keeps, drops or reorders pages into a new file. Originals are never changed.

pptx_tools.Description: PowerPoint decks (.pptx): read_pptx opens one slide by slide with notes, write_pptx builds one from Markdown (one '# Title' per slide, bullets, tables, pictures, speaker notes). The first write takes about a minute while ARI sets itself up.

xlsx_tools.Description: Excel workbooks (.xlsx): read_xlsx opens one (sheet, range, find), write_xlsx creates one from CSV-style text with formulas, edit_xlsx sets cells, appends rows and adds sheets. The user's own workbook is never changed in place; edits go to a copy.
